common_name: Gloire des Rosomanes Rose (Ragged Robin, Crimson China-Bourbon)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Gloire des Rosomanes is an 1825 French China-Bourbon hybrid, also known as Ragged Robin, grown for its vigor, heavy fragrance, and near-continuous bloom in hot climates.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil, spacing bushes 3-4 feet apart to accommodate its vigorous, somewhat lax growth. Gloire des Rosomanes bears semi-double, intensely fragrant crimson-red blooms in large clusters from spring through frost, and its toughness and disease resistance made it a popular understock and hedging rose throughout the 19th century. Prune lightly in late winter to control size and remove weak or crossing canes; it tolerates poor soil and heat well once established but flowers more heavily with regular water and feeding.

common_name: Papa Hemeray Rose (Single Cherry-Red Bicolor China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Papa Hemeray is an early 20th-century French China rose grown for its large single blooms and continuous flowering habit.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil enriched with compost, spacing plants 2.5-3.5 feet apart. Papa Hemeray produces large single flowers in bright cherry-red with a white-and-pink reverse and a prominent boss of golden stamens, opening in flushes almost continuously from spring to frost. Like other China roses it is notably heat- and disease-tolerant, performing well with minimal spray input in humid climates. Prune lightly in late winter to shape and remove dead wood, since heavy pruning sacrifices flowering wood and reduces bloom.

common_name: Oakington Ruby Rose (Dwarf Ruby-Red Miniature China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall; Oakington Ruby is an English dwarf China rose from the 1930s, one of the early parents behind many modern miniature roses.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, spacing dwarf plants about a foot apart along a border edge, rock garden, or container. Oakington Ruby bears small, double, deep ruby-red flowers that fade to pink-violet tones with age, carried in profusion on a tidy, very low, twiggy mound of tiny dark green leaflets. It blooms repeatedly from spring through fall with minimal care and is useful as an edging rose or in troughs and pots. Prune lightly in late winter to remove dead twigs and keep the compact habit tidy.

common_name: Irene Watts Rose (Dwarf Shell-Pink China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Irene Watts is an 1896 French dwarf China rose valued for its compact habit and near-constant bloom.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil, spacing plants about 1.5-2 feet apart. Irene Watts bears fully double, shell-pink to cream flowers that age toward soft rose, held in small clusters just above a dense, low mound of fine-textured foliage. It flowers in continuous flushes from spring through frost and stays compact without the hard pruning larger China roses need. Light shaping in late winter is all that is needed to keep the bush neat and encourage fresh flowering growth.

common_name: Sophie's Perpetual Rose (Fragrant Cerise-Pink Antique China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Sophie's Perpetual is a rediscovered English antique China rose valued for its strong fragrance and vigorous, repeat-flowering habit.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil enriched with compost, allowing 3-4.5 feet between plants for its vigorous, somewhat sprawling growth. Sophie's Perpetual produces fully double, richly fragrant blooms that open cerise-pink and deepen toward purplish rose as they age, flowering in repeated flushes from late spring through frost. Its vigor and lax, arching canes suit it to being trained against a wall, fence, or pillar as well as grown as a large freestanding shrub. Prune in late winter mainly to remove dead or crossing wood, since it flowers on both old and new growth.

common_name: Miss Lowe's Variety Rose (Dwarf Blood-Red Antique China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Miss Lowe's Variety is a low-growing antique China rose preserved in old rose collections for its intense blood-red color.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil enriched with compost, spacing plants 2-3 feet apart. Miss Lowe's Variety bears loosely semi-double, deep blood-red flowers with little to no fragrance on a low, twiggy, compact bush, flowering in repeated flushes from spring through frost. Its naturally dwarf stature makes it useful at the front of a border or in a container, and like other China roses it shows good resistance to blackspot and powdery mildew in hot, humid climates. Prune lightly in late winter to remove dead wood and maintain its compact form.

common_name: Fun Jwan Lo Rose (Pink Found Antique China Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Fun Jwan Lo is a 'found' antique China rose preserved by old rose collectors and valued for its vigor and reliable repeat bloom.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, compost-enriched soil, spacing plants 3-4 feet apart for its vigorous, arching growth. Fun Jwan Lo bears semi-double, soft pink flowers in small clusters that open almost continuously from spring through frost, on a tough, disease-resistant bush typical of the China rose class. It tolerates heat and humidity well and needs little spray input to stay healthy. Prune lightly in late winter to shape the bush and remove dead or weak wood, since hard pruning reduces its naturally generous bloom.
